verdict.rationale: Cal.com/Cal.diy is marketed as a 100% MIT-licensed, fully open-source, self-hostable fork with 'no proprietary Enterprise Edition features' (cal-com-gh-1/2/3/4, cal-com-docs-43/48), and a runtime probe confirms a legacy Cal.com docker image does boot a working self-hosted instance (cal-com-probe-rt-2). However, concrete hands-on community evidence directly contradicts current self-hosting viability: Cal.com stopped publishing public Docker images and told users to build the image themselves (cal-com-comm-4, cal-com-comm-14, cal-com-comm-19), the docs now say self-hosting is 'strictly recommended for personal, non-production use' (cal-com-comm-15), the API itself cannot be self-hosted without paying (cal-com-comm-3), the docker-compose setup is broken/messy (cal-com-comm-11), and the Cal.diy fork had no published Docker tags at time of the runtime probe (cal-com-probe-rt-2) — with users describing this as a 'bait and switch' (cal-com-comm-15, cal-com-comm-16, cal-com-comm-18). Missing for 10: a working, currently-published self-host Docker image/instructions for Cal.diy, first-party confirmation that self-hosting is production-supported, and resolution of the API self-hosting restriction.
